questions: Do the movements occur in discrete episodes rather than being continuous throughout the day?
During the movements, are you fully aware of your surroundings?
Do you experience an abnormal sensation (such as tingling or a "wave") in the arm just before the movements begin?
Is there temporary weakness in the arm after the movements stop?
Can you briefly suppress the movements by an effort of will?
Do you feel an irresistible urge to make the movement just before it happens?
Do the movements ever spread to your face or leg on the same side?
Do the movements persist while you are asleep?
Did the problem begin before the age of 18?
Is there a family history of seizures or movement disorders?
Are you currently taking any medications, particularly for psychiatric or stomach conditions?
Have you ever had a stroke, head injury, or brain infection?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Post-traumatic non-dominant (right) supplementary motor area / contralateral frontal lobe focal motor seizures (Jacksonian-type manual automatisms), due to prior head trauma causing the left frontal encephalomalacia now generating the left frontal epileptiform activity.

Alternatives to still consider:
1. Frontal lobe epilepsy arising from a traumatic left frontal cortical dysplasia-type lesion adjacent to the encephalomalacia
2. Movement disorder (task-specific dystonia or focal action-induced dystonia) with coincidental post-traumatic structural change
3. Psychogenic non-epileptic spells with left frontal sharp waves being incidental post-traumatic findings
